classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicitly requested intercept method on equations in different forms, solve for each intercept and convert the resulting coordinates into a straight-line sketch.

content.prompt: Sketch these graphs by finding the $x$- and $y$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, substitute $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3(0)+y&=12\\y&=12\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, substitute $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3x+0&=12\\3x&=12\\x&=4\end{aligned}$$
Plot $(0,12)$ and $(4,0)$, connect them and extend the straight line.

spec.description: Arrowed axes and descending answer line with only the two source intercept labels; no grid or ticks.

answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, substitute $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0-y&=7\\-y&=7\\y&=-7\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, substitute $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}x-0&=7\\x&=7\end{aligned}$$
Plot $(0,-7)$ and $(7,0)$, connect them and extend the straight line.

spec.description: Arrowed axes and ascending answer line with intercept labels 7 and -7; no grid or ticks.

answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, substitute $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}4(0)-3y&=9\\-3y&=9\\y&=-3\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, substitute $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}4x-3(0)&=9\\4x&=9\\x&=\frac94\end{aligned}$$
Plot $(0,-3)$ and $\left(\frac94,0\right)$, connect them and extend the straight line.

spec.description: Arrowed axes and ascending answer line; stacked fractional x-intercept label and negative y-intercept label.
